terms.meaning: The rough middle point of an area, used here as a stand-in location.
The two numbers that give a place's position on the globe.
A short two-letter code for a country, such as US or GB.

sections.name: COUNTRY_CENTROIDS (part 1)
sections.title: Country center table, first half
sections.what: Lists the rough center coordinates and display names for many countries, keyed by two-letter code.
sections.why: Gives the map a fallback position for projects with only a country.
sections.watch_out: The United Kingdom appears under two codes, UK and GB, so both must be kept.

sections.name: COUNTRY_CENTROIDS (part 2)
sections.title: Country center table, second half
sections.what: Continues the list with more countries, including several in Eastern Europe, Africa, and Asia.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are countries present in the project data.
sections.watch_out: The table ends at a closing brace, so any new entry must go above it.

sections.name: resolveCountryCode
sections.title: Finding a country code
sections.what: Turns a country name or code into the matching two-letter code, trying an exact code, an exact name, and then a partial name.
sections.why: Project data may store countries as names or codes, so both must work.
sections.watch_out: Partial matches can be wrong, for example a shorter name found inside a longer one.

sections.name: getProjectCoords
sections.title: Choosing a project's map position
sections.what: Returns the exact coordinates of a project when they exist, and otherwise the center of its country.
sections.why: Exact positions are better, so they are used first.
sections.watch_out: A project with no coordinates and no matching country gets no position and will not appear on the map.

summary: A lookup table of the rough center point of many countries, and helpers that convert a country name or code into map coordinates.
purpose: Lets a project appear on a map even when it has no exact location.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The approach is a fallback: exact coordinates first, then a country center.
how: Looks up a country by code. If not found, it compares the name with the table, then tries a partial match. A helper returns exact coordinates when present, and otherwise the country center.
inputs: A country code or name, and a project's optional latitude, longitude, and country.
outputs: A country code or a latitude and longitude pair, or nothing if no match is found.
risks: Partial matching can pick the wrong country. For example, the text Niger matches Nigeria. Many countries are missing from the table.
debug: If a project appears in the wrong place, check the country text it was given and the matched code. If it does not appear, the country may be missing from the table.
